To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Six Sigma programs must be designed with an understanding of the level of technological and electronic-business intensity in the firm.
the relationships between Six Sigma program design and SCA, and the relationship between Six Sigma program applications to electronic-business and SCA, are moderated by technological intensity.
Six Sigma program design, e-business practices, and SCA are moderated by the level of technological-intensity of the organization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of Six Sigma design factors and applications of Six Sigma programs to electronic business for high and low-tech organizations.
the impact of Six Sigma programs on SCA and the role of technological intensity in moderating the impact of design factors and electronic-business applications on SCA.
the moderating effect that technological intensity of a company has on the relationships among program design, electronic-business applications, and the resulting SCA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
high-technology firms have different relationships among program design factors and electronic-business applications, which lead to SCA than low-tech firms.

high-tech companies are better able to implement and benefit from Six Sigma programs that are designed to enhance process improvement and electronic-business applications, as compared with low-tech organizations.
Six Sigma program design and e-business applications have a greater effect on SCA for high technological intensity firms than for low technological intensity firms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the implementation of Six Sigma program design and e-business applications are associated with S CA.
Six Sigma design, and electronic-business applications are related to SCA for high-technological intensive firms, and that these relationships are moderated by technological intensity.
Six Sigma programs are perceived as being more successful in high-tech firms, and that the success of the Six Sigma program is related to the level of R&D investment in the organization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the level of technological investment of an organization must be considered to design Six Sigma programs to achieve competitive advantage.
high technological intensive firms are likely to attach greater importance to design factors that are more related to e-business practices than low technological intensive firms.
Six Sigma programs must be customized to the specific needs of the firm and that the level of technological investment of the company is one of the key factors to be considered in this customization.
